XR2206.name: XR2206

pins.name: AMSI
pins.eli5: Amplitude-modulation input. A voltage here turns the output up and down.

pins.name: STO
pins.eli5: Sine or triangle wave output: the sound leaves here.

pins.name: MO
pins.eli5: Multiplier output. The resistor here sets how big the wave is and where it rests.

pins.name: TC1
pins.eli5: Timing capacitor, one side. The bucket that fills and empties sits between pins 5 and 6.

pins.name: TR1
pins.eli5: Timing resistor 1. The resistor from here to ground is the faucet that sets the pitch (f = 1 ÷ RC).

pins.name: TR2
pins.eli5: Timing resistor 2. A second faucet, picked instead of pin 7 by the FSK pin.

pins.name: FSKI
pins.eli5: Frequency-shift keying input: chooses pin 7's faucet or pin 8's.

pins.name: BIAS
pins.eli5: Internal reference voltage. A capacitor here keeps it calm.

pins.name: SYNCO
pins.eli5: Square-wave sync output. It is open collector, so it needs a pull-up resistor to VCC.

pins.name: WAVEA1
pins.eli5: Waveform adjust 1. Leave 13 and 14 open for a triangle; join them through a resistor for a sine.

pins.name: SYMA1
pins.eli5: Symmetry adjust 1: trims how even the wave's halves are.

inside.eli5: A voltage-controlled oscillator plus a shaper: one part fills and empties a bucket to make a triangle, the next rounds it into a sine, and a buffer hands it out.
inside.detail: The datasheet lists four blocks: a VCO whose speed follows the current drawn from pin 7 or 8, an analog multiplier and sine shaper, a unity-gain buffer, and current switches that pick between the two timing resistors (that is the FSK trick).

XR2206.logic: Analog: it makes smooth waves, not just on and off.
XR2206.standard: Standard, off the shelf, with a public datasheet. Not bespoke.
XR2206.lineage: Made by Exar (later part of MaxLinear). Exar stopped making it; what you buy today is almost always a clone.
XR2206.buying: Watch for fake or clone XR2206s. Atommaker flagged this, and EEVblog forum threads describe clones with a weak, spiky sine or that get unstable above about 11 to 12 V. Use a socket so you can swap chips.

buyingLink.label: EEVblog: Don't buy any kit with XR2206

datasheet.label: Exar XR-2206 datasheet (Rev 1.04, hosted by SparkFun)

CD40106.name: CD40106B

pins.name: G = Ā
pins.eli5: Gate A output: the opposite of pin 1.

pins.name: J = D̄
pins.eli5: Gate D output. Note the flip: on this side the output comes before the input.

pins.name: F
pins.eli5: Gate F input. Unused inputs must be tied high or low, never left floating.

inside.eli5: Six Schmitt-trigger inverters: six doormen who only flip when the crowd passes a high line or a low line. Put a resistor from a doorman's output back to his input and a capacitor to ground, and he flips forever: an oscillator.
inside.detail: Each gate outputs the opposite of its input, with hysteresis: it switches high-to-low at a higher voltage than low-to-high. That gap is what lets one gate, one resistor and one capacitor make a square wave (the TI datasheet shows this astable circuit).

CD40106.logic: A logic chip: CMOS digital gates built to say only high or low. Here it is used as an analog oscillator, because a gate plus a resistor plus a capacitor squares out a steady beat.
CD40106.standard: Standard, off the shelf, with a public datasheet. Not bespoke.
CD40106.lineage: Part of the CD4000-series CMOS logic family (started by RCA). TI makes the CD40106B; other makers sell the same part as 40106 or MC14106.
CD40106.buying: Cheap and easy to find. The 74HC14 does the same job at low voltages only (about 6 V maximum), so it is not a drop-in for a 9 V circuit. CMOS chips dislike static: touch something grounded first.

TL072.name: TL072

pins.name: 1OUT
pins.eli5: Op-amp A's output: the bigger copy comes out here.

pins.name: 1IN−
pins.eli5: Op-amp A's minus input. Feedback from the output comes back here and sets the gain.

pins.name: 1IN+
pins.eli5: Op-amp A's plus input: the signal it copies.

pins.name: VCC−
pins.eli5: The bottom supply. On a 9 V pedal this is ground; on a ± supply it is the negative rail.

pins.name: 2IN−
pins.eli5: Op-amp B's minus input, where its feedback lands.

pins.name: VCC+
pins.eli5: The top supply: + 9 V on a pedal.

inside.eli5: Two op-amps in one package: two tireless copy machines that make whatever their plus input does, as big as their feedback allows.
inside.detail: JFET inputs draw almost no current, so the TL072 barely loads what feeds it. That makes it a favorite for buffers, filters and mixers in pedals and synths.

TL072.standard: Standard, off the shelf, with a public datasheet. Not bespoke.
TL072.lineage: Texas Instruments' TL07x JFET-input family (the datasheet dates from 1978). The TL082 is a close cousin with the same pinout.
TL072.buying: Easy to find and cheap. Any standard dual op-amp with the same 8-pin layout (TL082, NE5532, 4558) usually fits, but they differ in noise, current draw and tone.

pins.name: 1OUT
pins.eli5: Op-amp A's output: the bigger copy comes out here.

pins.name: 1IN−
pins.eli5: Op-amp A's minus input. Feedback from the output comes back here and sets the gain.

pins.name: 1IN+
pins.eli5: Op-amp A's plus input: the signal it copies.

pins.name: VCC−
pins.eli5: The bottom supply. On a 9 V pedal this is ground; on a ± supply it is the negative rail.

pins.name: 2IN−
pins.eli5: Op-amp B's minus input, where its feedback lands.

pins.name: VCC+
pins.eli5: The top supply: + 9 V on a pedal.

inside.eli5: Two op-amps in one package, like the TL072, but with older bipolar inputs.
inside.detail: In the Tube Screamer one half is the clipping amp with the diodes in its feedback, and the other half is the active tone stage.

RC4558.standard: Standard, off the shelf, with a public datasheet. Not bespoke.
RC4558.lineage: The JRC4558 from New Japan Radio is the famous Tube Screamer chip; TI makes the RC4558, which has the same pinout.
RC4558.buying: Easy to find. 'Vintage JRC4558D' is a collector's myth with a price tag; current 4558s work.

NE5532.name: NE5532

pins.name: 1OUT
pins.eli5: Op-amp A's output: the bigger copy comes out here.

pins.name: 1IN−
pins.eli5: Op-amp A's minus input. Feedback from the output comes back here and sets the gain.

pins.name: 1IN+
pins.eli5: Op-amp A's plus input: the signal it copies.

pins.name: VCC−
pins.eli5: The bottom supply. On a 9 V pedal this is ground; on a ± supply it is the negative rail.

pins.name: 2IN−
pins.eli5: Op-amp B's minus input, where its feedback lands.

pins.name: VCC+
pins.eli5: The top supply: + 9 V on a pedal.

inside.eli5: Two quiet, strong op-amps in one package.
inside.detail: It drives low-impedance loads well and draws more current than a TL072.

NE5532.standard: Standard, off the shelf, with a public datasheet. Not bespoke.
NE5532.lineage: First made by Signetics, now made by TI and others.
NE5532.buying: Easy to find. Draws more current, so a battery runs down sooner.

LM386.name: LM386

pins.name: GAIN
pins.eli5: Gain setting. Pins 1 and 8 open: gain 20. A capacitor from 1 to 8: gain 200.

pins.name: −INPUT
pins.eli5: Minus input. Often grounded when the signal goes into pin 3.

pins.name: +INPUT
pins.eli5: Plus input: the sound to make louder.

pins.name: VOUT
pins.eli5: Output to the speaker (through a big capacitor).

pins.name: BYPASS
pins.eli5: Bypass: a capacitor here keeps supply hum out.

inside.eli5: A small power amp: it turns a weak wiggle into enough push to move a speaker cone.
inside.detail: Unlike an op-amp it has its own fixed feedback inside (gain 20). Bypassing the internal 1.35 kΩ resistor between pins 1 and 8 raises the gain up to 200, per the TI datasheet.

LM386.standard: Standard, off the shelf, with a public datasheet. Not bespoke.
LM386.lineage: First made by National Semiconductor, now made by TI.
LM386.buying: Easy to find. Give it its speaker capacitor and a 10 Ω + 47 nF network at the output if it squeals.

NE555.name: NE555

pins.name: TRIG
pins.eli5: Trigger: when this dips below a third of the supply, the output goes high and timing starts.

pins.name: RESET
pins.eli5: Reset: pull it low to force the output low. Tie it high if unused.

pins.name: CONT
pins.eli5: Control voltage: moves the two trip points. A small capacitor here keeps them still.

pins.name: THRES
pins.eli5: Threshold: when this rises past two thirds of the supply, the output goes low.

pins.name: DISCH
pins.eli5: Discharge: a switch that empties the timing capacitor.

inside.eli5: Two comparators, a flip-flop and a drain switch: two lifeguards watch the bucket's water level, one shouts at the top line and one at the bottom, and a memory switch remembers who shouted last and opens or closes the drain.
inside.detail: A resistor divider sets the lines at one third and two thirds of the supply. The flip-flop drives the output and the discharge transistor. A monostable pulse lasts about 1.1 × R × C.

NE555.logic: Mixed: analog comparators that drive a digital flip-flop.
NE555.standard: Standard, off the shelf, with a public datasheet. Not bespoke.
NE555.lineage: First sold by Signetics around 1971, now made by TI and many others. Probably the most-made chip ever.
NE555.buying: Easy to find. The CMOS versions (TLC555, LMC555) use less current and make fewer supply spikes.

NE556.name: NE556

pins.name: VCC
pins.eli5: Power supply, shared by both timers.

inside.eli5: Two 555 timers in one package, sharing power and ground.
inside.detail: Each half has its own comparators, flip-flop and discharge switch. The pin order is not the same as two 555s side by side; check the datasheet.

NE556.logic: Mixed: analog comparators that drive a digital flip-flop.
NE556.standard: Standard, off the shelf, with a public datasheet. Not bespoke.
NE556.lineage: The dual version of Signetics' 555, now made by TI and others.
NE556.buying: Easy to find. Two separate 555s do the same job if you prefer 8-pin chips.

PT2399.name: PT2399

pins.name: REF
pins.eli5: Analog reference, half the supply. A capacitor keeps it steady.

pins.name: CLK_O
pins.eli5: System clock output (handy for measuring the delay clock).

pins.name: VCO
pins.eli5: VCO frequency adjustment. The resistor from here to ground sets the clock, so it sets the delay time.

pins.name: CC1
pins.eli5: Current control 1 (the datasheet's name). Wire it as the application circuit shows.

pins.name: OP1-OUT
pins.eli5: Op-amp 1 output, used as the modulator's integrator with a capacitor.

pins.name: OP2-IN
pins.eli5: Op-amp 2 input, used as the demodulator's integrator.

pins.name: LPF2-OUT
pins.eli5: Low-pass filter 2 output: the smoothed echo comes out here.

pins.name: LPF1-IN
pins.eli5: Low-pass filter 1 input: the dry sound goes in here first.

inside.eli5: A tiny digital tape loop: it turns sound into a stream of numbers (ADC), parks them in memory (44 kbit RAM), and turns them back into sound a moment later (DAC). The clock speed sets how long they wait.
inside.detail: Per the datasheet: a high-rate ADC writes a bit stream into internal RAM, a DAC and low-pass filter turn it back into audio, and an internal VCO clock (set by the pin 6 resistor) sets the delay. The datasheet table runs from about 31 ms to 342 ms.

PT2399.logic: Mixed: analog filters around a digital memory. It is the digital chip in an otherwise analog echo.
PT2399.standard: Standard, off the shelf, with a public datasheet. Not bespoke.
PT2399.lineage: Made by Princeton Technology (Taiwan), originally for karaoke echo. Pedal builders adopted it.
PT2399.buying: Buy from pedal-parts shops you trust; remarked and reject parts turn up. It needs its own 5 V supply.

LM565.name: LM565

pins.name: −VCC
pins.eli5: Negative supply (the CA-9 runs on ± supplies).

pins.name: PHASE COMPARATOR VCO INPUT
pins.eli5: Feeds the oscillator into the phase detector. Usually wired to pin 4.

pins.name: VCO CONTROL VOLTAGE
pins.eli5: Phase detector output, also the VCO's control voltage.

pins.name: TIMING RESISTOR
pins.eli5: The faucet that sets the oscillator speed.

pins.name: TIMING CAPACITOR
pins.eli5: The bucket that sets the oscillator speed.

inside.eli5: An oscillator and a balanced phase detector in one chip. A balanced detector is a multiplier at heart, so one chip can be both the carrier and the ring modulator.
inside.detail: The datasheet describes a VCO, a double-balanced phase detector with good carrier suppression, and an amplifier. The loop can be broken between the VCO and the detector, which is how a ring mod can use the parts separately.

LM565.standard: Standard part with a public datasheet, but discontinued.
LM565.lineage: National Semiconductor; discontinued. New-old stock and clones are around.
LM565.buying: Hard to find new. Check the seller and test it in a socket.
